title: sdks: unify auth/retries/streaming ergonomics across python/typescript/go and bump to v1.44.0
author: Maya Chen
description: Unify authentication, retry/backoff semantics, and streaming ergonomics across the three official SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go). Motivation: parity drift between SDKs has caused integration bugs and inconsistent developer experience for customers using multi-language stacks. This PR consolidates shared behaviors into SDK-specific adapters backed by the same design doc (ENG-3241): 1) centralize token refresh/auth middleware with pluggable credential providers, 2) standardize retry policy default (exponential backoff with jitter, 3 retries, idempotency hinting), and 3) provide a consistent streaming API surface: unified callback/async iterator ergonomics, cancelation semantics, and error propagation. The change set includes implementation + tests + docs and a version bump to v1.44.0 for all three SDK packages. Non-goals: internal server behaviour and transport protocol are unchanged. This description contains design notes, testing summary, and upgrade guidance. See below for files changed summary and reviewer notes.

release_notes:
- SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go) bumped to v1.44.0
- Unified auth middleware and credential adapter (better token refresh parity and pluggable providers)
- Standardized retry policy defaults: exponential backoff with jitter, 3 retries (configurable)
- Streaming API ergonomics unified: consistent iterator/callback patterns, cancelation semantics, and improved error propagation
- Migration guide added at docs/sdks/migration-v1.44.0.md
upgrade_guidance: For most users this is non-breaking. If you provided custom retry policies or relied on previous lower-level streaming behavior, follow docs/sdks/migration-v1.44.0.md. Key callouts: 1) retry defaults changed to 3 attempts - reduce if you rely on fewer retries, 2) streaming now exposes cancel() / context support - ensure you close iterators where appropriate, 3) TokenProvider adapters are available if your provider is synchronous in Python.
notes: This PR was coordinated across sdks team and merged as part of the v1.44.0 umbrella release. Post-merge: created follow-up task ENG-3320 to monitor streaming E2E flakiness and ENG-3321 to add an additional canary using the new streaming ergonomics.
